short: FERASEC is a standard engineered radar front end with a large gain over 2016 features; phoneme novelty holds only for consonant syllables, and evaluation is within-speaker.
position: The paper changes the radar feature front end (M06), which is standard for the field and well supported against the authors' 2016 baseline, but its case against learned front ends rests on raw frames fed to a DNN-HMM and is contradicted, on one participant and 50 words, by the first author's later network on the same testbed. The first-phoneme claim holds only as contactless classification of consonant syllables, since silent vowel classification with contactless IR-UWB radar predates it. Evaluation (M12) is within-speaker leave-one-out without seeds or spread, with words and phrases from 4 speakers; placement results confound position with antenna and distance, and device integration is not measured.
